headline: Six of seven majors above the 200-day line with overbought momentum, but whales are moving $1.2B onto exchanges this week while spot ETF bids persist.
paragraphs: The regime is decisively above trend. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, and ADA all trade above their 200-day moving averages; only Dogecoin sits below. No golden crosses have formed, meaning the 50-day lines have not yet recrossed above the 200-day lines, but the underlying positioning is firmly bullish across the board. All seven assets print MACD above their signal lines, confirming momentum alignment with the uptrend. The spread of above-trend assets across market cap tiers (Bitcoin at 59.2% dominance) means this is not a rotation within a sideways market; this is broad acceptance of higher ground.

Momentum readings are uniformly overbought and show minimal divergence from trend. Bitcoin's RSI-14 stands at 81.8, Ethereum at 77.4, Solana at 86.2, and BNB at 80.9. These are extreme readings, typically associated with extended moves. Yet the price action does not contradict them: Bitcoin has moved up 1.25% on the day and 24.06% over the week; Solana is up 6.86% on the day and 43.53% over the week; XRP is up 2.25% on the day but 45.1% over the week. These gains are real, not noise. The tension is not between momentum and trend but between overbought readings and the continued absence of a 200-day golden cross. An RSI in the 80s for days on end without a 50/200 cross suggests either that the move is far stronger than the simple moving average framework captures, or that the move is nearing a resting point where the cross may finally resolve.

Derivatives positioning shows mixed signals. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding has turned negative at negative 0.0016%, annualizing to negative 1.8%, which means long positions are paying shorts to hold. Yet Bitcoin's long/short ratio sits at 0.96, indicating a slight short bias in open interest of $2.21 billion. Ethereum prints a positive 0.0007% 8-hour funding (annualized 0.8%) with a long ratio of 1.19, the market leaning long; $1.49 billion is at stake. Solana, the week's strongest performer, carries negative 0.0025% 8-hour funding (annualized negative 2.8%) despite a 1.13 long ratio and $373 million open interest. Dogecoin stands out: its funding is positive 0.0043% 8-hour (annualized 4.7%), and its long/short ratio is the highest in the set at 3.58. Liquidations over the last 13 to 24 hours show shorts being cleared far more than longs across most assets: Bitcoin saw $9.07 million in short liquidations versus $3.97 million in longs; Solana saw $8.86 million in shorts versus $2.26 million in longs. This pattern suggests shorts are under pressure, but the elevated funding rates on Bitcoin and Solana hint that the mood to hold long bets is becoming expensive.

Whale flow data reveals a critical divergence. Over the last 48 hours, $169.87 million moved onto exchanges net, a neutral-to-cautious posture. But the weekly breakdown is starker: the week ending August 27 saw $1.216 billion move onto exchanges, the largest weekly inflow in the dataset. The week ending August 20 showed $223 million onto exchanges, and the week ending August 13 showed $761 million onto exchanges. Only the week ending August 6 saw net outflow (off exchanges) at $812 million. The recent three weeks are heavily skewed toward selling. Within the 48-hour window, Ethereum saw a one-directional flow of $170.24 million onto exchanges; Bitcoin flows were mixed, with $181.2 million in and $181.6 million out, nearly balanced. The biggest single moves to exchanges are concentrated at Coinbase and Coinbase Institutional: $68.4 million BTC, $67.5 million ETH, and $59.0 million BTC. Meanwhile, the biggest moves off exchanges are BTC from Binance ($62.9 million) and Coinbase itself ($59.5 million and $59.1 million). This pattern suggests some whales are holding through institutional channels while others are tactically exiting positions to the bid.

Spot ETF flows stand in contrast to whale behavior. Bitcoin spot ETFs printed $232.2 million inflow on August 26 and $1.798 billion net inflow over the last five sessions, with flows in the same direction for eight consecutive days. Ethereum spot ETFs printed $192.4 million inflow on August 26 and $891.3 million net over five sessions, also with eight consecutive days of same-direction buying. This is traditional-finance capital voting with its feet. Stablecoin reserves sit at $309.24 billion, up just 0.77% over the last 30 days, meaning dry powder is flat. The gap between ETF inflows and whale onto-exchange moves suggests that institution-grade capital from the ETF market is buying dips that whales are selling into.

The Fear & Greed gauge reads 71 (Greed territory) after a 30-day range of 25 to 74, suggesting the crowd has shifted from panic to confidence. Yet the tape shows nuance. Funding rates are mixed, liquidations favor longs in most assets but not overwhelmingly, and the largest asset flows are moving onto exchanges while ETF demand persists. Watch for three conditions: a flip in Bitcoin's funding from negative to positive, which would signal long confidence hardening; a 200-day golden cross in any major asset, which would confirm the trend shift is mature; and a reversal in weekly whale flows from onto-exchange to off-exchange, which would signal the big money is reinvesting rather than reducing. Until one of those materializes, the market is in a state of broad bullish positioning but uncertain about its own durability.
